title: Windows & Siding — Why More Companies Are Choosing Not to Build Their Own Teams
content:
###  **A Shift Worth Noticing** 

Across the window and siding trade, more companies are moving away from building their own field teams and toward working with structured programs already built for this kind of outreach. 

###  **What's Driving the Shift** 

The reasons tend to repeat: turnover in field roles is high, training takes longer than expected, and managing a team pulls time away from running the actual business. 

### **The High-Ticket Factor** 

Windows and siding are big-ticket, infrequent purchases — decisions homeowners make once every decade or more. That makes the trust and recognition built through consistent presence especially valuable, and especially costly to build inconsistently. 

###  **The Practical Alternative** 

Rather than building and managing a team internally, a structured territory program lets these companies access the same kind of consistent presence without the internal overhead.
